Clean the package caches of condathis

Source: R/clean_cache.R
clean_cache.Rd

Removes the package and metadata caches of condathis and of every registered backend, and nothing else:

  • For the built-in micromamba backend, the package cache, pkgs, and the repodata cache, cache, in its data directory (see get_install_dir()).

  • For every other backend, its own package and metadata caches, and conda-pkgs in its data directory. conda-pkgs is the package cache of the Conda tools that run in its environments (see Child processes in register_backend()).

  • The contents of the condathis cache directory, tools::R_user_dir("condathis", "cache").

clean_cache() never deletes the per-user caches of conda, mamba and micromamba, such as ~/.cache/conda, which other tools share.

Usage

clean_cache(verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"))

Arguments

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. It also shows these messages and this warning when they occur (see condathis-conditions):

  • condathis_micromamba_downloading (a message): no usable micromamba was found, so it is downloaded. Queries, such as list_envs(), never download it.

  • condathis_env_lock_waiting and condathis_cache_lock_waiting (messages): the call waits for another R session.

  • condathis_install_micromamba_checksum_unavailable (a warning): the checksum of the downloaded micromamba could not be checked.

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose. The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

Value

A condathis_result object, invisibly: a classed list with status, stdout, stderr, timeout, pid, cmd and env_name. The values come from the micromamba command that ran, and cmd is its command line. When no micromamba command ran, status is 0, timeout is FALSE and the other fields are NA. pid is always NA, and so is env_name: the caches are not tied to an environment.

Details

Environments keep the files of their packages. These files usually share disk space with the package cache through hard links. You free that space only by also removing those environments (see list_envs() and remove_env()).

When the micromamba package cache does not exist, micromamba has nothing to clean. clean_cache() then starts no process and does not install micromamba. It still deletes the repodata cache and clears the condathis cache directory.

clean_cache() loads a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, when its data directory has caches or environments. When that package is not installed, clean_cache() does not clean its caches and warns with class condathis_backend_not_installed.

clean_cache() waits until no other R session creates an environment or installs packages. Those sessions wait until it is done (see Other R sessions in create_env()).

When a backend fails to clean its caches, clean_cache() still cleans the caches of the other backends and the directories above. Then it aborts with the first failure. That error has the classes condathis_clean_cache_failed and condathis_backend_error, and the error of the backend as its parent. When clean_cache() cannot delete a directory itself, it aborts with class condathis_clean_cache_failed the same way.

Removing everything

clean_cache() keeps micromamba and the environments. To remove everything that condathis installed, delete its data and cache directories, in an R session that runs no condathis command at the same time:

unlink(condathis::get_install_dir()$path, recursive = TRUE)
unlink(tools::R_user_dir("condathis", "cache"), recursive = TRUE)

The condathis data directory, the path of the "micromamba" row of get_install_dir(), holds the micromamba binary that install_micromamba() downloaded, every environment, the package and repodata caches, the lock files and the configuration file that condathis writes for micromamba. The data directories of the other backends that use backend_root_dir() are inside it. get_install_dir() also lists the data directory of a registered backend that chose its own.

This leaves alone what condathis did not install: a micromamba that condathis found elsewhere (see micromamba discovery in condathis-options), environments that you passed as env_path(), the lines that micromamba added to ~/.conda/environments.txt, the pip cache on macOS and Windows (see get_install_dir()), and on Windows the Start Menu shortcuts that condathis 0.1.4 and earlier added (see remove_env()).

See also

condathis-conditions for every condition class.

Other setup: get_install_dir(), get_sys_arch(), install_micromamba(), micromamba_bin_path(), with_sandbox_dir()

Examples

condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  condathis::clean_cache(verbose = "output")
})
#> ✔ Cache successfully removed.
